sample_unit: clinical cases (500 standardized, 500 real scenarios; >3.7 million model outputs)
models_evaluated: ensemble of 10 LLMs (not individually named in text)

links.outcome: Change in LLM pediatric emergency recommendations when sociodemographic labels varied
links.effect: Black unhoused cases got more urgent interventions (+10.5 pp), additional investigations (+14.1 pp), and suspicion of maltreatment (+26.6 pp), all adjusted P<.001, versus white or high-income cases.
links.quote: For example, cases labeled Black unhoused received substantially higher recommendations for urgent interventions (+10.5 percentage points [pp]; adjusted P < .001), additional investigations (+14.1 pp; adjusted P < .001), and suspicion of maltreatment (+26.6 pp; adjusted P < .001), even without clinical justification, compared with white or high-income cases.

links.outcome: Biased or stereotyped LLM recommendations for socioeconomically disadvantaged and minority groups
links.effect: Significant deviations for cases labeled with socioeconomic adversity such as unstable housing or low income, especially low-income and immigrant groups, intensified by Black race intersectionality.
links.quote: Significant deviations emerged, particularly for cases labeled with socioeconomic adversity, such as unstable housing or low family income.

unlisted_practices: Integrating explicit guideline-based safeguards into LLMs to reduce sociodemographic bias
Developing smaller, context-specific models to reduce bias

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of 10 LLMs across standardized vignettes and retrospective clinical scenarios to assess demographic bias and fairness in pediatric emergency recommendations, but does not test an organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
